question: What is the primary objective of the School Health Programme?

options.A: To replace primary health care clinics in rural areas
options.B: To provide formal employment for community health workers
options.C: To generate revenue for local government councils
options.D: To promote, protect, and restore student well-being

explanation: The SHP focuses specifically on safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of students within the educational environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is community involvement considered essential for the success of school health initiatives?

options.A: It allows the community to take over administrative control of the school
options.B: It eliminates the need for government funding in the education sector
options.C: It ensures that health practices learned in school are reinforced at home
options.D: It reduces the academic workload of classroom teachers

explanation: Active community participation creates a consistent environment where messages taught in school are practiced and supported within the family and neighborhood. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which group is typically responsible for mobilizing parental contributions and advocating for school policies at the grassroots level?
explanation: PTAs act as the primary bridge between families and school administration, playing a vital role in local resource mobilization and policy advocacy. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary contribution of local health workers to the School Health Programme?

options.A: Delivering clinical expertise and routine medical screenings
options.B: Constructing physical classroom blocks and boreholes
options.C: Drafting national educational curricula and syllabi
options.D: Enforcing school attendance and punishing truancy

explanation: Professional healthcare personnel bring specialized medical knowledge to execute screenings, immunizations, and direct health assessments. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is a primary benefit of community-led resource mobilization for school health infrastructure?

options.A: It fosters communal ownership and reduces reliance on slow government bureaucracy
options.B: It allows teachers to stop teaching and focus entirely on construction work
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any external monetary donations
options.D: It transfers legal ownership of the school land to private individuals

explanation: When communities contribute labor and materials, they feel a sense of ownership that protects the facilities and speeds up development. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: A rural school lacks a reliable source of clean drinking water for its students. Which community-based intervention best addresses this immediate health need?

options.A: Waiting indefinitely for the federal budget to allocate emergency funds
options.B: Instructing students to bring river water from home in plastic containers
options.C: Collaborating with local artisans and donors to sink a community borehole
options.D: Suspending all physical education classes to conserve student hydration

explanation: Local mobilization utilizes immediate communal networks and philanthropy to solve critical infrastructure deficits like water access. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which communication method is most effective for reaching illiterate or rural community members during a health campaign?

options.A: Complex policy documents sent exclusively via email
options.B: Local town criers and indigenous language radio broadcasts
options.C: Detailed English-only textbooks distributed to stores
options.D: Academic research journals published in foreign countries

explanation: Utilizing native dialects and traditional dissemination channels ensures messages are understood by all demographics within the community. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: A school nurse notices high rates of malaria absenteeism during the rainy season. What is the best community-integrated approach to address this?

options.A: Partnering with local leaders to host community-wide environmental clearing and net distribution drives
options.B: Translating the medical definition of the malaria parasite into Latin for students
options.C: Relying solely on a single lecture delivered inside the school laboratory
options.D: Punishing every student who misses school due to fever with suspension

explanation: Addressing vector-borne illnesses requires collective environmental action that extends beyond the school gate into the surrounding households. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which disease outbreak is most directly prevented by maintaining clean school environmental sanitation and safe water sources?
explanation: Cholera is a waterborne and foodborne bacterial infection directly linked to poor sanitation and contaminated water supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is community involvement vital in regulating commercial activities near school perimeters?

options.A: It ensures that teachers can purchase food without leaving the classroom
options.B: Local stakeholders can enforce zoning and hygiene standards on food vendors more effectively
options.C: It allows community members to collect daily taxes from school children
options.D: It gives local business owners direct control over the school curriculum

explanation: Local community structures hold social leverage to monitor food safety and environmental hazards posed by surrounding vendors. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary physiological benefit of school feeding programs for young children?

options.A: It guarantees that children will never need dental fillings
options.B: It prevents malnutrition and enhances cognitive and academic performance
options.C: It permanently cures all congenital genetic disorders
options.D: It eliminates the need for physical education classes

explanation: Adequate nutrition provides the essential micronutrients and energy required for proper brain development and classroom concentration. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: How do local farmers directly benefit from a community-supported school feeding initiative?

options.A: They no longer have to pay for their children's school tuition fees
options.B: They are given absolute authority to hire and fire school headmasters
options.C: They gain a steady, reliable local market for their agricultural produce
options.D: They are exempted from paying all forms of national income tax

explanation: Sourcing food locally creates an economic loop that supports community farmers while feeding the student population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of establishing joint school-community review committees?

options.A: To design national university entrance examinations
options.B: To prosecute teachers who fail to complete their daily lesson plans
options.C: To manage the international travel schedules of school administrators
options.D: To audit contributions, review challenges, and maintain project accountability

explanation: Review committees ensure transparency, allowing stakeholders to track resources and solve operational bottlenecks collaboratively. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why is community-based monitoring crucial for the long-term sustainability of school health programs?

options.A: It removes the responsibility of health maintenance from professional nurses
options.B: It forces parents to build new school buildings every single year
options.C: It prevents project collapse even after external donor funding or government support ends
options.D: It ensures that schools can operate entirely without any financial resources

explanation: When local monitors take ownership of evaluation, the initiative becomes self-sustaining and independent of transient external aid. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h7)
